guides.title: Welcome to Mihur — How It Works
guides.summary: A tour of Mihur and how its learning approach works.
guides.body:
# Welcome to Mihur — How It Works

Mihur is a mathematics learning space built to help students understand ideas before memorizing procedures. A parent manages the family account; each child can use a private practice link to work in their own learner space.

**Pilot note:** Some features are implemented but still being independently tested. Your family's available curricula and tools depend on what the pilot team has approved. If a topic says **Content in progress**, it is not yet ready to practice.

## Choose your path

- **Parents:** Start with the [Parent Quick Start](/help/parent-first-day) to create your account, add your child and share a link.
- **Students:** Try the [Student Quick Start](/help/student-first-session) to begin learning independently.
- **Educators:** Read [How Mihur Teaches](/help/progress-and-mastery) to understand the approach. A dedicated educator account or classroom dashboard is not included in this pilot guide.
- **Questions or concerns:** See [Privacy, Safety & FAQs](/help/privacy-and-faq).

## How learning works

Mihur aims to move from **concrete objects → visual models → mathematical symbols**. Depending on the approved skill, a learner may explore a model, work through a problem, receive a guiding question, or complete a fresh independent check.

The teaching sequence is **Observe → Predict → Manipulate → Explain → Practice → Diagnose → Transfer → Verify**. Not every lesson includes every interactive tool, and a practice answer is not automatically proof of mastery.

## Who does what?

**Parent or guardian:** Registers/signs in, creates a four-digit Parent PIN, chooses the family's location, creates one learner profile per child, manages private practice links, and unlocks progress and sensitive settings.

**Student:** Opens their own private link, chooses a ready topic, works through problems, requests help during eligible guided work, and builds independent evidence. Students do not need their own email or password.

**Mihur:** Uses application-owned mathematical checks and approved content to support learning. AI may help phrase selected hints; it is not the trusted grader or decision-maker for mastery.

## Start here

[Set up your family in about ten minutes](/help/parent-first-day) or [see the student's first practice session](/help/student-first-session).

For what information Mihur handles, read the [Privacy Practices](/privacy) page. For urgent account/access problems, contact the pilot team using the private support channel supplied with your invitation; do not send practice links or student records to an unknown address.

guides.title: Parent Quick Start — Your First 10 Minutes
guides.summary: Create your account, add learners and share private practice links.
guides.body:
# Parent Quick Start — Your First 10 Minutes

This guide follows the parent registration, practice, settings and PIN controls currently present in Mihur's application. It is written for selected pilot families, not open public enrollment.

## Before you begin

You need an invitation or enrollment instructions from the Mihur pilot team, access to your email account, and the state/province and grade appropriate for each child. Use nicknames or aliases instead of children's full legal names.

**Pilot availability:** Registration may require a single-use invitation code and staff approval. If your account is awaiting approval, do not create another account; contact the pilot team.

## 1. Create your parent account

1. Open the approved Mihur site or your invitation link. Choose **Create account** if the registration form is not already open.
2. Enter your parent email, a strong password, and an optional parent display name.
3. Set your **four-digit Parent PIN**. This is separate from the sign-in password; it unlocks sensitive parent settings and detailed progress views.
4. Select your country and state/province. Read and accept the terms and family privacy notice, and complete the anti-bot challenge if shown.
5. Submit. If you see an approval/waiting state, follow the instructions from the pilot team rather than trying again with a different email.

**Keep your Parent PIN private.** Do not share it with a child. A child's own private link is how they enter practice.

## 2. Add a child

1. As the parent, open **Practice** at [/learn](/learn).
2. In **Add a learner**, enter a short learner nickname, select an avatar and choose an available **exact curriculum** matching the child's grade and school pathway.
3. Select **Add learner**. Repeat for each child your approved pilot entitlement allows.
4. If your region or curriculum isn't available or an option shows **Content in progress**, ask the pilot team which accepted curriculum/skills your family should use. Do not select an unrelated grade merely to unlock more questions.

A child profile keeps learning activity and progress separate from siblings. Seat limits can vary by family pilot entitlement; the pilot does not require you to purchase a subscription.

## 3. Share each child's private practice link

1. Open **Parent → Settings & privacy** at [/parent/settings](/parent/settings).
2. Unlock the page with your four-digit Parent PIN if requested.
3. Under **Private practice links for each child**, find the correct nickname. Select **Generate link**.
4. Select **Copy private link** and send it **privately to that child's device**. The complete link is displayed only immediately after it is created.
5. Repeat separately for every child. Each child must use their *own* link; do not share a sibling's.
6. Links expire after **seven days**. If a link is lost, use **Regenerate link** to replace it, or **Revoke link** to disable it. Regeneration/revocation ends learner sessions created by that child's previous link, not siblings' links.

**Protect the link like a password.** Anyone holding it could attempt to open that child's practice area. Do not put links in public chats, screenshots or school-wide messages. If Mihur says a link is in use on another device, ask the child to finish or contact the parent to regenerate it.

## 4. Check your child's progress

1. Open [Parent dashboard](/parent).
2. Unlock the sensitive progress view using your Parent PIN.
3. Choose the child's profile and review learning activity, concepts needing support, reviews due, and independent progress.

A guided answer, a hint, a badge and a mastery check mean different things. See [Understanding Progress, Hints & Mastery](/help/progress-and-mastery).

## 5. Protect your family account

Review [Settings & privacy](/parent/settings) for privacy notices and parent-managed learner deletion. Deleting a learner's data is different from revoking a link; follow the on-screen confirmation carefully. Sign out of parent accounts on shared devices.

For account problems, see [Privacy, Safety & FAQs](/help/privacy-and-faq). Never send us your password, PIN or full practice-link token.

**Screenshots:** Real first-day screenshots will be added after independent QA captures the current interface using synthetic family accounts. This guide intentionally does not use illustrative images that could be mistaken for real screens.

guides.title: Student Quick Start — Your First Practice Session
guides.summary: Your first Mihur practice session, step by step.
guides.body:
# Student Quick Start — Your First Practice Session

Hi! Welcome to Mihur. You don't have to know every answer already. You are here to discover how the math works.

## 1. Open your own link

Ask your parent or grown-up for **your Mihur practice link**. Open it in your browser. You won't need a student email or password. Your learner space should open directly.

If the link is expired, has been changed or says someone is already using it, ask your parent for help. **Never use a brother's or sister's link.**

## 2. Pick something ready to learn

On the **Practice** page, look for **Explore Topics**. Find a skill marked **Ready to practice**. If it says **Content in progress**, that topic isn't ready yet.

Choose a topic. You may see **Learn this first**, a model or a quick check. When you're ready, choose **Start learning**. A quick placement check can help Mihur look for earlier ideas you may need.

## 3. Think, try, and show your work

- **Observe:** What do you notice in the problem or picture?
- **Predict:** What do you think could happen?
- **Manipulate:** Try changing or arranging parts of an available model.
- **Explain:** Tell yourself why a step works. Writing a useful step matters.
- **Practice:** Answer a question and check what the feedback says.

Some questions let you type an answer. Others may offer a step-by-step work area, a scratchpad, or a visual activity, depending on the topic.

## 4. When you get stuck

It's okay to make mistakes. In guided practice, use **Hint** or **I don't understand** when those buttons are available. Mihur can ask a question that helps you spot what went wrong.

Try a new idea, not only the same answer. A mistake helps Mihur understand what support might be useful. If a hint isn't available, you might be doing a check meant to show what you can do **by yourself**.

## 5. Show what you know independently

After help and practice, Mihur may ask you to solve a fresh problem without hints. This is different from guided work. Doing well on a helped problem does **not** automatically count as independent mastery.

Look at your progress for what you've practiced and which ideas need another try. You can always return to [Practice](/learn) for another ready topic.

## Remember

**Thinking beats guessing.** A careful explanation, a changed strategy or a corrected mistake is meaningful progress.

Questions? Read [How Mihur Helps You Learn](/help/progress-and-mastery), or ask your parent to read [Help for Families](/help/privacy-and-faq).

**Screenshots:** Actual learner-interface images are pending independent synthetic-browser verification. No made-up product screenshots are shown.

guides.title: Understanding Progress, Hints & Mastery
guides.summary: Guided help, conceptual learning and independent mastery evidence.
guides.body:
# Understanding Progress, Hints & Mastery

Mihur is designed around one idea: a learner should understand *why* a method works, not only recognize the right number.

## Mihur's learning sequence

1. **Observe:** Read the situation and identify the known quantities.
2. **Predict:** Say what should happen before completing the calculation.
3. **Manipulate:** Build or change a picture, number line, fraction bar or other model **when that lesson supports one**.
4. **Explain:** Describe each transformation, including why both sides of an equation stay equal.
5. **Practice:** Try examples with helpful guidance.
6. **Diagnose:** Review the kind of error made, such as a missing negative sign or a skipped operation.
7. **Transfer:** Try a different but related problem rather than repeating a memorized response.
8. **Verify:** Solve independently and check the result using valid mathematical reasoning.

A specific lesson may use only a subset of these steps. Additional interactive models are still under review; an authored lesson description does not mean its visual has been activated.

## Helped success versus independent evidence

During **Guided Practice** or **Remediation**, a learner may receive a question, clue or visual scaffold. That is teaching support. It is not the same as demonstrated mastery.

During **Independent Practice** or a **Mastery Check**, Mihur must use the approved, trusted answer and mode checks. Hints or guided successes do not qualify as independent evidence. A fresh check helps test whether understanding transfers to a new problem.

A progress percentage or badge can encourage practice, but it does not by itself establish readiness for every topic. Parents should focus on recurring strengths and misconceptions, not one score.

## What parents can see

The [parent dashboard](/parent) includes activity and progress views for linked children; detailed views require a Parent PIN. Depending on accepted content and actual practice, it may include attempts, concepts requiring support, reviews due and independently verified mastery.

A low number of practice questions or a topic marked **Content in progress** can indicate that material is not ready in your child's selected curriculum. It does *not* prove that your child has a learning difficulty.

## What AI does — and does not do

Mihur's application-owned mathematical logic determines valid answers, approved learning states and mastery eligibility. Constrained AI services may help phrase explanations or hints. They do **not** independently grade answers or override mastery rules. If a provider is unavailable, built-in guidance can serve eligible lessons.

## A good conversation after practice

Instead of only asking **“How many did you get right?”**, ask:

- “Can you show me why that works?”
- “What changed when you tried another method?”
- “What would you do if the numbers were different?”

For your child's first login, use the [Parent Quick Start](/help/parent-first-day). For privacy questions, see [Privacy, Safety & FAQs](/help/privacy-and-faq).

guides.title: Privacy, Safety & Frequently Asked Questions
guides.summary: Private links, family controls, privacy and common questions.
guides.body:
# Privacy, Safety & Frequently Asked Questions

Mihur is designed so **parents manage family accounts** and children practice through private learner links, without a child email or password. Only use approved pilot access instructions and keep sensitive family information out of support messages.

## Who needs an account?

A parent or guardian creates and signs in to the family account, with a separate **four-digit Parent PIN** for sensitive views. Each child has their own nickname-based learner profile and private practice link. Parents can create, replace or revoke links for their linked children.

## What information does Mihur handle?

The public [Privacy Practices](/privacy) page describes the categories handled by Mihur, including parent account information, learner nicknames, curriculum/grade selection and practice evidence. **Learn Together** may store drawings, typed notes or homework images for a board. Avoid uploading school records or identifying details where possible.

Mihur states that AI helps phrase hints while trusted mathematical checks remain in application code. Review the published privacy notice before consent; the Help Center is informational and is not a legal certification of COPPA compliance.

## What if my child's private link stops working?

It may have expired (typically seven days after generation), been revoked, replaced or been used on another device. Ask the parent to open **Parent → Settings & privacy**, unlock with their PIN and **Regenerate link** for *that child*. A regenerated link replaces only that child's old link.

## Can two children share the same link?

**No.** Each child should receive their own practice link and use their own device/browser session. One student's history must not be attributed to a sibling. Parents should avoid using parent sign-in and child practice on the same shared device without signing out and checking which account is active.

## Why can't I open a topic?

Some curricula or mathematical families are still under independent review. On **Explore Topics**, only select skills marked **Ready to practice**. Content that is unpublished or provisional should not be unlocked by selecting a similar-looking skill from another grade or state.

## Can Mihur simply tell my child the answer?

Mihur is designed to build understanding. In eligible guided practice, it may ask helpful questions or show a representation. A mastery check is meant to provide independent evidence, so guided hints must stay separate.

## How do I see progress or delete a learner?

Sign in as the parent and use [Parent dashboard](/parent) for progress or [Settings & privacy](/parent/settings) for parent controls. A deletion is irreversible and differs from revoking a pass. Do not share your PIN.

## Is the Learn Together whiteboard available?

The application contains a family whiteboard with handwriting, text and photo/PDF import routes. **Pilot availability and live multi-device reliability are subject to staging WebSocket, privacy and independent browser QA.** Ask the pilot team whether your family has been approved to use it. Do not treat it as independently assessed mathematics; it is a collaborative workspace.

## Where can I get support?

Use the invitation or pilot communication channel supplied directly by the Mihur team. Include the approximate time, page name, browser type and a description of what happened, but **never send** passwords, PINs, full private links, another student's work or identifying child information.

Return to [Welcome to Mihur](/help/welcome) or read the [Parent First-Day Guide](/help/parent-first-day).
